text:
kevin: heads-up — our new RAG sample (Next.js + LlamaIndex) flaked in evals today. Scoring varies across runs.
anita: what changed? new sample commit or infra?
kevin: sample uses @redwood/sdk@0.10.2 (node). Repro: POST /api/rag/embed with 5 items, sometimes response missing an id and once we got a duplicate when a 401 happened mid-batch.
sue: logs?
kevin: pasted snippet: ```
req ids: [i1,i2,i3,i4,i5]
responses seen: [i1,i3,i2,i5]
auth error on chunk 2 -> retry returned [i2]
merged: [i1,i3,i2,i5,i2]  // i4 missing, i2 duplicated
```
matt: aha — two issues: unordered fill (promises resolving out of order) and retry merge appending duplicates. Python SDK dedupes by client id. Node doesn't.
anita: quick sample workaround? we need deterministic output for evals.
kevin: added a tiny reassemble helper in api/embed.ts that maps by item.id and reorders to input sequence + dedupe. Set SAMPLE_RAG_STABLE=true in .env for CI.
devex-bot: created issue #2034 in sdk repo  labels: sdk,bug,parity
matt: I'll prototype a JS SDK fix: allocate placeholder array, fill by index as results arrive, and on retry write into original slots while ignoring duplicate ids. Expose opt-in `preserveInputOrder` (default true for parity).
sue: please include a unit that simulates a 401 mid-batch and asserts final set has same ids and order, no duplicates. Add an eval harness test too.
anita: opened samples PR with workaround + README note: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/8142 — CI preview failed because harness detected ordering diffs, so gate is necessary.
kevin: also noticed KV-cache prefixing in the sample (for embedding caching) can hide missing items — watch for cache TTL interactions in tests. I added a note in the sample README.
matt: will bench perf at 200 qps to quantify overhead. If <5% we can keep preserveInputOrder default.
devex-bot: preview deploy for pr/8142 rolled back  reason: ci/tests:eval-harness failed
anita: thanks — tracking in the SDK issue, will remove SAMPLE_RAG_STABLE once SDK fix lands and add an integration test to prevent regressions.
